questions.q: Someone suffering matters more than someone being wronged.
Cruelty is the worst thing a person can be.
People should get out what they put in — no more, no less.
Standing by your own people counts, even when they are wrong.
Respect for those in charge holds a society together.
Some things are degrading even when nobody is harmed.
Being told what to do is a harm in itself.
Rules I never agreed to have no hold on me.
Toughness does more good than tenderness.
I would put a month of savings into something volatile.
I read the fine print before signing anything with money in it.
I skip the check-up and assume it is nothing.
I will say the unpopular thing in a room that disagrees.
Steep, fast and slightly out of control is my idea of fun.
I would bend a rule if the outcome were clearly better.
Most people would give back a wallet they found.
You have to be careful — people take advantage.
For one group to gain, another has to lose.
Trade between countries leaves both better off.
In the long run, people get roughly what they deserve.
Where you end up is mostly where you started.
€100 today beats €160 in a year.
I plan further ahead than most people I know.
I finish the boring part first and enjoy the rest after.
If I want it, I buy it — I sort the rest out later.
A decade from now feels real enough to save for.
Waiting is easy when I know what is coming.
I would rather try an unknown dish than order the one I love.
I rewatch and relisten to the same things for years.
A film that needs a second viewing is a better film.
Earnest beats clever.
If everyone likes it, it has usually been sanded down.
I keep up with what most people are watching.
I say it in the room rather than after.
I let small things go to keep the peace.
I would rather win the argument than end it.
When it heats up I go quiet and leave.
I joke to make a room easier to be in.
When things go badly I can usually find it funny.
A good joke is worth someone being stung by it.
I get laughs by putting myself down.
A joke that needs a target isn’t worth telling.
My first instinct is usually right.
I want the numbers before I decide.
I change my mind when the evidence changes.
Sitting with not knowing is uncomfortable.
My choices are mine before they are my family’s.
What my community expects shapes what I do.
Breaking a social rule should have consequences.
Places work better when people are left to improvise.
